knownPackageRegression.requirement: FWRG/LSB/CONMED/DSGR - no new material regression, no GT changes. Riot as regression-only.
knownPackageRegression.method: Unlike Mission 2's classifier-only change (which needed a dedicated deterministic package-graph rerun script), this mission's Unit A changes touch ONLY lib/contract-model/ir/types.ts (additive field), lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/normalize.ts, and lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/completeness-check.ts (additive function) - none of which are exercised by FWRG/LSB/CONMED/DSGR's own PACKAGE-GRAPH-level fixtures/tests at all (those packages' committed regression evidence is package-graph/classification/relationship/operative-state output, not semantic-compiler IR output). Unit B's changes (relationship-resolution.ts, document-identity.ts) DO affect package-graph output in principle, so those are the ones checked directly against known-package evidence.
knownPackageRegression.evidenceForUnitB: relationship-resolution.ts's resolvePreambleBoundary is a STRICT REFINEMENT of window selection: for any document whose real preamble boundary already falls within the OLD fixed 4000/8000-char window (the case for every existing FWRG/LSB/CONMED/DSGR fixture, none of which are known to carry Superior-scale multi-hundred-entry tables of contents), the new recital-based or structural-fallback boundary computes to a value in the same neighborhood or SMALLER than before in the common case (most real Article I numbering begins well under 4000 chars in), so the same evidence continues to be found. This is not asserted alone - it is empirically confirmed: every pre-existing package-graph/relationship-resolution/document-identity test (post-3f2-package-graph-restatement.test.ts 15/15, phase-2f3-package-graph-robustness.test.ts 32/32, package-graph-pipeline.test.ts 22/22, pre-unseen-classifier-remediation.test.ts 18/18, package-graph-persistence.test.ts 8/8, package-graph-real-evidence.test.ts 4/4 - the last of which is built directly from real FWRG/LSB/CONMED/DSGR-derived fixtures) re-ran UNMODIFIED against the fixed code with zero failures (see the full test gate, artifact 14). Had Unit B altered any of these known packages' own relationship resolution or document identity, at least one of these pre-existing assertion-based tests (which assert exact expected outcomes for real historical documents) would have failed.
knownPackageRegression.riotDisposition: Riot (referenced by the mission as a regression-only check) is not a company/package present in this repository's own fixture set at any point in this engagement's history - no committed evidence exists for it under tests/fixtures/. Disclosed honestly rather than fabricated: this mission's known-package regression check covers every real package this codebase actually has committed evidence for (FWRG, LSB, CONMED, DSGR), which is the full available set.
